title: Keep decay out of the gradient moments
description: A quick reference for the adaptive-moment, bias-correction, and decoupled-decay terms used here.

terms.definition: An adaptive optimizer combining moment-normalized gradient updates with separate parameter decay.
An exponentially weighted estimate carrying recent gradient direction across steps.
An exponentially weighted estimate of recent squared gradient magnitude by coordinate.
An adjustment compensating for early moment estimates that start at zero.
A parameter change scaled coordinatewise using corrected direction and magnitude estimates.

Parameter-proportional shrinkage applied outside the gradient moments used for adaptation; for positive decay, the represented product of the learning rate and decay coefficient must be finite and strictly between zero and one.

A positive scalar controlling adaptive and decay contributions; multiplied by a positive decay coefficient, it must produce a represented result strictly between zero and one, while zero decay is explicit.
A small positive denominator addition keeping adaptive division well defined.
Named parameters selected to receive the optimizer's shrinkage contribution.
Named parameters deliberately excluded from parameter-proportional shrinkage during updates.
